messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the pinning RFC — we need to pick a behavior for implicit pin resolution in the client surface. Two competing patterns came up in the doc: server-driven sticky pins vs client-side implicit resolves with soft-fallbacks. Thoughts?

kevin: tl;dr: I prefer server-driven sticky pins for safety (single source of truth) but worried about control plane coupling and latency for first requests.

anya: Agreed on safety. Also: client implicit resolve lets SDKs short-circuit on-device without an extra control-plane call, which helps mobile/offline. But it pushes complexity into many SDKs.

thad: Can we do a hybrid? Client does quick local resolution using "last-known-pin" header, then control-plane can assert/override async. If mismatch, client receives a soft-notify and can rebind.

riley: Example flow I sketched: client sends X-Pin-Hint header, runtime accepts or returns X-Pin-Resolution:sticky|accepted|override. If override -> client retries once. Minimal extra RTT in common case.

maria: Nice. We should also model leases/ttl: implicit pins should carry a lease token so control plane can evict after TTL and clients can detect stale hints. Example metadata payload:```json
{"pin_hint":"model-v3.2.1","lease":"lease_abc123","expires_at":"2026-09-01T16:00:00Z","source":"client-hint"}
```

kevin: Two tradeoffs: 1) telemetry — we must surface whether client-hints caused safe fallbacks so SRE can alert on churn. 2) migration — older SDKs won't send hints. Need default server behavior that doesn't regress tail latency.

anya: For migration I'd prefer server default to respect tenant-level affinity config: tenants can opt into implicit-hint acceptance via a flag. That avoids surprising global behavior changes.

thad: Can we encode acceptance rules in rollout metadata? e.g., rollout_metadata.accepts_client_hint = true/false and rollout_metadata.hint_tolerance = 0.05 (fraction of requests allowed to diverge).

maria: Yes — that gives ops control. Also propose a canary header: X-Client-Hint-Canary that only active SDKs set when doing gradual enable. Server increments telemetry counter by route/model.

riley: One more: how to expose to customers? Console UI should show "client-hint acceptance" per model version with counts for accepted/overridden. Add a small warning when acceptance rate drops below threshold.

kevin: Security question: any PII risk in pin hints? We should sanitize and limit hint fields to stable model identifiers (no prompt data). Also sign leases with KMS so runtime can validate authenticity.

maria: Good call. Implementation plan proposal:
- Phase 1: Add X-Pin-Hint header and server-side acceptance/override responses behind feature flag. Telemetry counters + lease token prototype.
- Phase 2: SDKs add optional hint emission and canary flag. Console shows acceptance metrics. Tenant opt-in toggle.
- Phase 3: Lease signing + stricter validation, rollout of default-on for supported tenants.

anya: Sizing note: control-plane load only increases for first requests or when hints mismatch. If we accept local-hint path as default fast path, load should be small. But we need a small autoscaling buffer when toggling feature flags.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature/implicit-pin-hint branch built and pushed to staging (build 2026.5.9-142). :rocket:

maria: Action items: @kevin to write compatibility note for SDKs, @anya to mock console UI metric, @thad to add rollout_metadata fields in schema draft, @riley to add telemetry counters and log docs. I'll open a short PR with the phased plan and sample header docs.

kevin: I'll draft SDK guidance. Quick question: do we want the header name to be X-Pin-Hint or Redwood-Pin-Hint? I lean Redwood-Pin-Hint to avoid collisions.

anya: Redwood-Pin-Hint. Also include X-Client-Hint-Canary as opt-in.

maria: Cool — I'll update the RFC follow-up and tag infra and SDKs. Thanks everyone. :)
